result.summary: This residential intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including zebra-marked crosswalks, traffic signals, and continuous sidewalks. However, safety is reduced by wide crossing distances and parked vehicles that obstruct sight lines at the corners.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars near the intersection corners, such as the black SUV, block the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground corner near the crosswalk

hazards.name: Prohibited Pedestrian Crossing
hazards.description: A sign prohibits crossing on one leg of the intersection, which can lead to unsafe mid-block crossings or inconvenient detours for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection on the signal pole

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sight lines for both pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide multi-lane roadway with a marked crosswalk and pedestrian signals. However, the long crossing distance without a median refuge and the wide lane geometry suggest a high-speed environment that increases pedestrian exposure and risk.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to cross a significant distance without a refuge island, increasing exposure time to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the center of the roadway

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb can block the sightlines between pedestrians entering the crosswalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway along the curb

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines.

result.summary: The intersection features a wide, multi-lane arterial road with significant crossing distances and a lack of visible pedestrian markings. While sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the environment is dominated by high-speed vehicle infrastructure with no clear, protected path for pedestrians to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalks
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks visible at this large intersection, leaving pedestrians without a designated or predictable path.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the foreground and the main arterial road

hazards.name: Excessive crossing distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a long duration without dedicated protection.
hazards.location_in_image: The multi-lane road (Roosevelt Blvd) in the background

hazards.name: Missing pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible to indicate when it is safe to cross the multi-lane road.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian paths and increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce the crossing distance and improve sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: This is a high-speed arterial environment with a 40 mph speed limit and multiple travel lanes. While sidewalks are present, the intersection lacks marked crosswalks across the main roadway and visible pedestrian signals, creating a significant barrier for safe crossing.

hazards.name: High Vehicle Speeds
hazards.description: A posted speed limit of 40 mph significantly increases the risk of fatal injury in the event of a pedestrian collision.
hazards.location_in_image: Speed limit sign on the left side of the roadway

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing at Signalized Intersection
hazards.description: Despite being a signalized intersection, there are no marked crosswalks across the main arterial, leaving pedestrians without a designated path.
hazards.location_in_image: Main intersection area in the center of the image

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals which may not provide adequate crossing time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks on all legs of the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on remaining crossing time.

interventions.description: Program the signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.
